name: Local Process Models
description: Discovers Local Process Models: small, frequently-recurring Petri-net fragments over a subset of a log's activities, each possibly firing several times within one trace. A recursive process-tree search (sequence/choice/parallel/inclusive-choice/loop operators) scored by alignment-based support, confidence, determinism, language fit and coverage — ported from Tax, Sidorova, Haakma & van der Aalst's LocalProcessModelDiscovery. Also covers object-centric event logs: discovers per object type, then merges structurally matching fragments across types and flags variable arcs.

citation.text: Tax, N., Sidorova, N., Haakma, R., van der Aalst, W.M.P. (2016). Mining Local Process Models. Journal of Innovation in Digital Ecosystems, 3(2), 183-196. Object-centric extension after Porsil, M. (RWTH Aachen, PADS), ObjectCentricLPMs.

actions.label: Discover Local Process Models
actions.description: Recursive process-tree search over a subset of the log's activities, scored by alignment-based support, confidence, determinism, language fit and coverage.

agent.whenToUse: The user wants recurring sub-patterns within a bigger, possibly spaghetti-like process — a small fragment that occurs several times per trace, not a whole-process model.
agent.notFor: Discovering the overall control-flow of the process — use Inductive Miner, Heuristics Miner or Alpha Miner for that.
examples: numTransitions 4, frequencyMinimum left at its auto default for a first look

numTransitions.title: Max fragment size
numTransitions.description: How many expansion steps a candidate fragment may go through — each sequence/choice/parallel/inclusive-choice step adds one activity, a loop step adds none. Bigger finds more elaborate patterns but the search space grows fast.

topK.title: Results kept
topK.description: How many ranked fragments to keep.

maxActivities.title: Activity limit
maxActivities.description: Keeps only the most frequent activities before searching — the search space is exponential in the alphabet size, so this (not a clustering/projection scheme) is how a wide-alphabet log stays tractable.

frequencyMinimum.title: Min support (occurrences)
frequencyMinimum.description: A fragment must occur at least this many times across the log (case-weighted) to be kept, and this also prunes the search early — no candidate activity below this can ever raise a fragment's support back up.

determinismMinimum.title: Min determinism
determinismMinimum.description: 1 / average number of transitions enabled at each step while replaying the fragment — closer to 1 means the fragment leaves little ambiguity about what happens next.

languageFitMinimum.title: Min language fit
languageFitMinimum.description: Fraction of the fragment's own possible behavior that was actually observed in the log — a guard against fragments that could do far more than they were ever seen doing.

confidenceMinimum.title: Min confidence
confidenceMinimum.description: Harmonic mean, over the fragment's own activities, of how much of each activity's total log occurrences this fragment accounts for.

coverageMinimum.title: Min coverage
coverageMinimum.description: Fraction of the whole log's events that belong to this fragment's own activity set.

duplicateTransitions.title: Allow repeated activities
duplicateTransitions.description: Lets the same activity appear at more than one position within one fragment.

useOr.title: Inclusive choice
useOr.description: Enable the inclusive-choice (∨) expansion operator — do at least one of two activities, any order. Off by default, matching the reference implementation.

useXorLoop.title: Loop
useXorLoop.description: Enable wrapping a single activity in a repeat-or-exit loop (↻).

maxSearchMillis.title: Search time budget (ms)
maxSearchMillis.description: The search runs depth-by-depth and returns the best fragments found so far once this is spent, flagged in the result rather than silently cut off — there is no thread pool inside a Wasm worker, so this (not parallelism) is what keeps the tab responsive.

maxAlignStates.title: Alignment state cap
maxAlignStates.description: Safety bound on the alignment search per candidate fragment against one trace variant.

maxLoop.title: Language enumeration bound
maxLoop.description: How many times a single transition may fire while enumerating a fragment's own possible behavior for the language-fit metric.

actions.label: Local Process Model → Petri Net
actions.description: Recompiles one ranked fragment back into a plain Petri net fragment, viewable with any Accepting Petri Net renderer.

index.title: Fragment rank
index.description: Which ranked fragment (0 = top) to convert.

objectType.title: Object type
objectType.description: Flattens the log by this object type — each object of this type becomes one trace. Left empty, the single most frequent object type is used.

optionsFrom.sql: SELECT object_type AS value, COUNT(*) AS n FROM {object} GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY n DESC

actions.label: Discover Local Process Models (object-centric)
actions.description: Discovers Local Process Models for one object type: flattens the OCEL by that type (one trace per object), then runs the same recursive process-tree search as the traditional action. Run once per object type, then combine the results with "Combine Local Process Models across object types".

agent.whenToUse: The user wants recurring sub-patterns in an object-centric event log, scoped to one object type at a time.
agent.notFor: A single run across every object type at once — this action always scopes to exactly one object type per run; combine multiple runs afterward for a multi-type fragment.
examples: objectType set to the log's leading/case-defining object type for a first look

objectType.title: Object type
objectType.description: Which object type to discover Local Process Models for — the log is flattened by this type (one trace per object) before searching. Left empty, the single most frequent object type is used.

optionsFrom.sql: SELECT object_type AS value, COUNT(*) AS n FROM {object} GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY n DESC

actions.label: Combine Local Process Models across object types
actions.description: Merges two per-object-type Local Process Model sets (from "Discover Local Process Models (object-centric)") into object-centric fragments: structurally matching patterns across the two types are merged into one multi-type fragment, and (activity, object type) pairs where the activity often relates to more than one object of that type are flagged as variable arcs.

agent.whenToUse: The user has already run object-centric discovery for two object types and wants one combined, object-centric result.
agent.notFor: A first discovery pass — run "Discover Local Process Models (object-centric)" once per object type first.
examples: variableArcThreshold left at its 0.95 default, matching ObjectCentricLPMs

inputs.name: setA
inputs.label: a per-object-type Local Process Model set

inputs.name: setB
inputs.label: another per-object-type Local Process Model set (different object type)

variableArcThreshold.title: Variable-arc threshold
variableArcThreshold.description: An (activity, object type) pair is flagged as a variable arc once at least this fraction of the activity's events relate to more than one object of that type.

actions.label: Local Process Model → Object-Centric Petri Net
actions.description: Recompiles one merged, multi-type fragment (from "Combine Local Process Models across object types") into an Object-Centric Petri Net, viewable with any Object-Centric Petri Net renderer.

inputs.name: set
inputs.label: a combined, object-centric Local Process Model set

index.title: Fragment rank
index.description: Which ranked (merged) fragment (0 = top) to convert.
